context:
The pipeline currently loads each bundle exactly once into memory to
build manifest + details. Extend that same pass: maintain a dict
keyed by (benchmark, scale_factor, phase) that accumulates platform
rows as each bundle is processed. At the end of the pass, emit one
BenchmarkSummary per key.

Do not refactor the pipeline architecture for this change. Add the
accumulator and the emission step. Nothing else.

For phase handling: schema-v2 bundles already carry a `test_type`
("power" or "throughput"). Use that field to route each platform row
into the right accumulator bucket. Bundles without an explicit
test_type default to "power" (matches current CLI behavior).
description:
The strategy review (2026-04-15) identified that the explorer's current
data model - manifest.json (aggregate only) + details/{id}.json (one file
per result) - cannot support a ClickBench-style Platform × Query matrix
leaderboard without N parallel detail fetches assembled client-side. That
approach is slow, fragile, and silently breaks when platforms run
heterogeneous query subsets.

This TODO introduces a third derived artifact shape emitted by the
explorer pipeline:

    results-explorer/public/data/benchmarks/{benchmark}_sf{sf}_{phase}.json

One file per (benchmark, scale_factor, phase) tuple, containing the full
cross-platform query matrix pre-computed from already-loaded bundles (no
extra I/O - the pipeline already has everything in memory during its
single pass).

Key schema decisions driven by the adversarial review:

1. Key includes **phase** (not just benchmark/scale). The proposal that
   keyed on (benchmark, scale) alone silently collapses power vs
   throughput vs maintenance phases. Making phase part of the filename
   makes the scope of each matrix explicit and URL-addressable.

2. Tuning_mode is a per-platform-row field, not an artifact-level filter.
   Two DuckDB rows with different tuning modes occupy different matrix
   rows; the UI labels them as such.

3. Each row carries `power_score` (for TPC-H/TPC-DS), `geomean_ms`, and
   `cost_usd` so the UI can choose ranking metric per benchmark family
   without a second fetch.

4. Sparse matrices: platforms that ran a subset of queries produce
   `null` in the missing cells, never crash the build.

5. Artifacts are gzipped on write (`*.json.gz`). TPC-DS SF100 with 30
   platforms × 99 queries × throughput streams can reach 200-500KB raw;
   gzip cuts that ~5×. Loader handles both for local dev convenience.

anti_patterns.dont: collapse tuning modes into a single row per platform
anti_patterns.instead: each (platform, tuning_mode) gets its own row
anti_patterns.why: tuned vs notuning is a comparability-breaking dimension

anti_patterns.instead: use null and document the fallback (display_geomean_ms)
anti_patterns.why: that would sort broken results to the top

anti_patterns.dont: fan out into additional bundle loads
anti_patterns.why: the pipeline is already O(N) bundles

anti_patterns.dont: key the artifact on (benchmark, scale) alone
anti_patterns.why: it silently mixes power and throughput phases

anti_patterns.dont: populate timings cells from the first raw QueryTiming row
anti_patterns.instead: use display_ms from QueryDisplayTiming (median of passing runs)
anti_patterns.why: the first row is the cold-cache outlier

anti_patterns.dont: use geomean_ms (raw all-sample) for display ranking
anti_patterns.instead: use display_geomean_ms from the read-model contract reduction
anti_patterns.why: it averages cold-cache and throughput-stream rows

anti_patterns.dont: use platform string directly as the matrix row key
anti_patterns.instead: use platform_id from the read-model contract
anti_patterns.why: it may include trust suffixes producing spurious duplicate rows

preserves.behavior: Existing details/{id}.json per-result pages - detail page consumers must continue to work
Existing manifest.json schema - new artifact is additive; do not remove or reshape manifest fields
ExplorerPipeline.run() remains a single pass over bundles - no extra bundle loads introduced

work_units.notes:
BenchmarkSummary fields: benchmark, scale_factor, phase, query_ids
(ordered), platforms (list of PlatformRow), cell_reduction (string
documenting the reduction policy, e.g.
"median_successful_measurement_ms"), ranking (from
RANKING_METRIC_BY_FAMILY, set by explorer-align-ranking-metric-with-tpc-standards).

PlatformRow fields:
  result_id, platform_id (canonical), platform (raw display name),
  platform_version, tuning_mode, tuning_hash, execution_mode,
  trust_label, run_date, is_ranking_eligible (bool),
  power_score (nullable), display_geomean_ms (from read-model contract
  display reduction - NOT raw geomean_ms), sample_geomean_ms (raw,
  for audit), cost_usd (nullable),
  timings (dict query_id → display_ms from QueryDisplayTiming, null
  per missing cell - NOT the first raw duration_ms row).

The distinction between display_geomean_ms and sample_geomean_ms is
critical: the matrix cells MUST use display_ms values (median of
passing runs per logical query), not raw per-sample rows. See
explorer-fix-read-model-contract for the reduction definition.
work_units.summary: Define BenchmarkSummary + PlatformRow Pydantic models in benchbox/core/explorer/models.py

work_units.notes:
Zero additional disk I/O - accumulate from detail results already
loaded in the single-pass scan. Phase values: "power" and
"throughput" in Phase 1. Use the same sf_str formatting as existing
manifest paths.

Canonical-row selection: for each (platform_id, benchmark, scale,
phase) group, call `select_canonical_row()` from the read-model
contract to pick the default ranked row. Non-canonical variants
(different tuning modes, trust tiers) are included as additional
PlatformRows marked `is_ranking_eligible: false`. This lets the
matrix default view show one row per platform while the "All
variants" filter reveals the full set.

Sort canonical rows first by `is_ranking_eligible` descending, then
by primary ranking metric (power_score or display_geomean_ms).
Non-eligible rows follow in the same metric order.
work_units.summary: Extend ExplorerPipeline.run() to emit benchmarks/{b}_sf{sf}_{phase}.json.gz per (benchmark, scale, phase) tuple

work_units.notes:
Cases: (a) normal multi-platform; (b) sparse query subset
(platform missing Q17 → null cell); (c) mixed tuning modes produce
distinct rows; (d) phase separation (power and throughput produce
separate files); (e) gzip output is valid and round-trips.
